facts.product: sonicdesk — a web workspace for bands ("version control for music"). This campaign promotes the Snippet feature: inside a song's mixer you select a 5–30 second part of the mix (presets 5/10/15/20/25/30 s or free drag), it snaps to section starts (Verse, Chorus, etc.), loops for listening, and exports as an audio file you can use to test the hook in Reels/TikTok before release.

tokens.voice.copyRules:
Product labels, meta and buttons are UPPERCASE mono with wide tracking (`meta`, `section-label`). Names, sentences, toasts and empty states are sentence case. The wordmark is always lowercase.

Keys short: C, Em, F#m — spelled by the song's key (flats in flat keys: Bb, Eb; sharps in sharp keys: F#, C#). Positions as bar.beat (41.3), durations m:ss (3:47), relative time "10d ago · yesterday · just now", older dates "Oct 4", sizes "112.3 MB · 50 GB".

tokens.imagery.treatment: Waveforms a drawn as pills, never rectangles: full-round bars with a 2px gap (3px on phones), height from the audio peaks with a 14–15% floor. brief.objective: Drive sign-ups from independent musicians and bands by showing one concrete, useful feature: cutting a short audio snippet of an unreleased song to test which part works as a hook on social media.

design.designDocument:
CONCEPT. Studio-gear black canvas (#070707), square corners, hairlines, one lime (#DFFF00) light. Headlines Archivo SemiBold uppercase (Noto Sans fallback in draft), tight tracking, ink #F8F8F8. Labels and meta in Noto Sans uppercase wide tracking, never under 32px. Waveform pills are full-round with a 2px gap (the only rounded shapes). No shadows on flow elements, no emoji, no competitor names. The product UI is never generated; the only product-like imagery is simplified code-drawn mockups (pills, ruler, playhead). Frame.tsx props: format, locale, hook, cta, length, sceneId, moment. Everything is static and final-looking; no playback.

BACKGROUND LAYER. Near-black with a 40px master grid of hairlines at about 6 percent ink. Optional dark photo layer (resources) at 35-55 percent under a black gradient so text keeps 4.5:1 contrast or more.

TYPE LAYER. Headline left-aligned, uppercase, Archivo, tracking -0.03em, leading 0.95. Size is about 120px vertical, 96px square and portrait, 112px wide. The headline is split on its sentences, one line per sentence. A lime full stop may close a line. Never colour a whole word lime unless it is the offer or CTA in scene 5.

SCENE 1 HOOK: LOST TRACK OF YOUR BEST TAKE? Dark rehearsal-room photo (resource 1) dimmed. The headline sits big in the lower-middle safe zone. Moment A: the full question in ink. Moment B: the same frame plus a few stray ghost pills at 15 percent ink scattered off-grid, feeling lost. A small lime dot marks one pill as the best take, outlined only. Motion later: hard cut in, slight handheld drift on the photo, pills jitter.

SCENE 2 PROBLEM: END THE CHAOS. KEEP EVERY VERSION. Desk-clutter photo (resource 2) at lower opacity as texture on the right or bottom. Line 1 in ink. Line 2 in ink with its full stop lime. Moment A: scattered, tilted file-name chips drawn as hairline rectangles with mono labels like take_07_final_FINAL (no emoji). Moment B: the chips snap onto the grid and align in a tidy column, same copy. Motion later: chips slide and snap, 40-50ms stagger, cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1).

SCENE 3 SOLUTION: SAVE. REVERT. COMPARE. INSTANTLY. Flat graphic hero: 4 stacked waveform-pill tracks (code-drawn, peaks floor 14 percent), each a version. Unplayed pills ink at 20 percent; played pills lime. A 1px lime playhead with a soft glow and a small triangle on a hairline ruler. The four verbs are set as stacked display-m lines in ink, with one verb per moment highlighted by a lime underline hairline. Resource 3 is a labelled video proxy for the sliding pills and the scrub. Moment A: pills in, playhead at about 30 percent. Moment B: playhead at about 70 percent, a different track highlighted. Motion later: pills grow 0.7s, 3-6ms apart, and the playhead scrubs across.

SCENE 4 BENEFIT: FOCUS ON THE MUSIC. WE HANDLE THE FILES. Photo (resource 4) of hands on an instrument beside a laptop, dark, shallow depth, on the upper half or right half. FOCUS ON THE MUSIC in ink, WE HANDLE THE FILES in ink at 100 percent with a lime full stop. A thin hairline strip of calm pills sits below as the quiet background work. Moment A: photo with line 1 only emphasised. Moment B: both lines, with the pill strip fully lime-played. Motion later: slow push-in on the photo, text slides in.

SCENE 5 CTA/OFFER. Black canvas, grid, and a pill-waveform band across the bottom or side at low opacity. The sonicdesk wordmark (supplied asset 93111854, placed exactly as drawn, with the supplied lime full stop; the icon 745244ea may sit as a secondary mark, never on lime). Offer: FREE 1ST MONTH BAND-PLAN THIS MONTH in lime. CTA button: a single lime-filled square button with near-black text SIGN UP, minimum 40px touch height and at least 32px text; the full stop is lime. Only the offer and the CTA are lime; when two things are lime, neither is, so the pills drop to ink at 20 percent here. Moment A: logo and offer. Moment B: the CTA button added, offer unchanged. Motion later: logo appears, text slides in, lime pulse on the CTA.

FORMAT ADAPTATIONS. Vertical 1080x1920: keep text inside top 192 and bottom 345.6 safe bands, stack everything in one column, photo on the top half with the type below. Square 1080x1080: 54px margins, headline 96px, photo as a full-bleed dim layer. Portrait 1080x1350: 54 and 67.5px margins, a column like vertical with a tighter pill hero. Wide 1920x1080: 96px side margins, two columns, type on the left 55 percent and photo or pills on the right, CTA bottom-left.

VARIANT AXES. Hook primary uses the supplied copy. hook-1 to hook-3 reuse the same layout with copy from the generated brand module. Length 6, 9, 12 and 15 only change the hold time per scene and the number of moments shown; the layout is unchanged. Locale en-GB, cta primary. Pills use 3px gaps on phones. Proxies are labelled and replaced later. Sound later: clean, precise cues, mechanical-confident, nothing theatrical.
